editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-banking city of about 831,000. Its retail is heavy on banks & atms and grocery & daily needs, and thin on cafés, tea & coffee and fitness & wellness — and 32% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 44% of Hyderabad's. 14.67 chain outlets per lakh residents against 33.58 in Hyderabad; 28 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 40, MedPlus 12, Reliance Smart / Fresh 8.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 4.8% (Hyderabad 3.1%); malls & department stores 1.0% (Hyderabad 0.7%); offices 6.0% (Hyderabad 10.9%); services & crafts 4.2% (Hyderabad 6.9%). Raw counts would mislead because Hyderabad is mapped more completely (62,819 places against 4,297), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 6 zones hold 32% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Vidyaranyapuri alone has about 50,000 residents and 8 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Hyderabad. 49% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Hyderabad 43%). The largest cores are Lashkar Bazar (916 places) and Mandi Bazar · Svn Road (643).

The widest brand gaps against Hyderabad. Apollo Pharmacy 40 outlets vs 348; MedPlus 12 outlets vs 150; Reliance Trends 7 outlets vs 89. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Hyderabad, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Mandi Bazar · Svn Road and Lashkar Bazar are the largest zones by residents (226,000 and 216,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 49% of all commercial places, and Lashkar Bazar alone lists 916.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Lashkar Bazar holds 38 of the 122 tracked chain outlets, and Mandi Bazar · Svn Road adds 32.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Lashkar Bazar and Mandi Bazar · Svn Road lead on education places (135 and 80, with 29 and 11 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Vidyaranyapuri and Deshaipet. The blue cores include Lashkar Bazar.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (62,819 places in Hyderabad against 4,297 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Hyderabad; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Hyderabad, Warangal's mapped places over-index on automotive (4.8% vs 3.1%), malls & department stores (1.0% vs 0.7%), banks & finance (11.6% vs 8.1%) and under-index on offices (6.0% vs 10.9%), services & crafts (4.2% vs 6.9%), other services (5.3% vs 7.6%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 122 outlets of 28 tracked national brands within 8 km — 14.67 per lakh residents against Hyderabad's 33.58 (1440 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Hyderabad are Apollo Pharmacy (40 vs 348); MedPlus (12 vs 150); Reliance Trends (7 vs 89). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Hyderabad's, so low means thin by Hyderabad's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Warangal's age mix against Hyderabad: children (0–14) 19.0% vs 24.6%, 15–24 19.5% vs 20.4%, working age 50.3% vs 48.0%, 60+ 11.3% vs 7.0%. Under-25s are 38% of residents.

zones.506002: Reasonably supplied: 643 places for about 226,000 residents (index 76), 32 chain outlets.
zones.506001: About 216,000 residents, 916 mapped places (retail depth index 113), 38 chain outlets.
zones.506009: An under-served zone: about 50,000 residents, 101 mapped places, 8 food & drink and 14 chain outlets. Depth index 54.
zones.506006: An under-served zone: about 49,000 residents, 27 mapped places, 1 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 15.
zones.506003: An under-served zone: about 39,000 residents, 81 mapped places, 9 food & drink and 5 chain outlets. Depth index 56.
zones.506004: An under-served zone: about 37,000 residents, 60 mapped places, 20 food & drink and 3 chain outlets. Depth index 43.
zones.506007: About 30,000 residents, 90 mapped places (retail depth index 80), 2 chain outlets.
zones.506370: An under-served zone: about 27,000 residents, 35 mapped places, 6 food & drink and 3 chain outlets. Depth index 34.
zones.506015: An under-served zone: about 26,000 residents, 32 mapped places, 3 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 33.
zones.506011: A commercial core: 101 mapped places and 3 chain outlets (2% of the city's tracked chains) for about 15,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 4.7% of mapped places against 5.0% in Hyderabad, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 5 (Hyderabad 85), Pizza Hut 3 (Hyderabad 41), KFC 2 (Hyderabad 49), McDonald's 1 (Hyderabad 34). No mapped outlet in either city: Biryani By Kilo, Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 1.4% of mapped places against 2.3% in Hyderabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Third Wave Coffee 1 (Hyderabad 2). No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.0% of mapped places against 0.8% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 1 (Hyderabad 29), Cream Stone 1 (Hyderabad 13).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.5% of mapped places against 2.1% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 8 (Hyderabad 42), DMart 6 (Hyderabad 26), Spencer's 2 (Hyderabad 14), Vishal Mega Mart 2 (Hyderabad 10). No mapped outlet in either city: Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.5% of mapped places against 1.3% in Hyderabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 40 (Hyderabad 348), MedPlus 12 (Hyderabad 150). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 5.9% of mapped places against 5.8% in Hyderabad, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Trends 7 (Hyderabad 89), Bata 5 (Hyderabad 70), Raymond 4 (Hyderabad 37), Tanishq 3 (Hyderabad 19).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 11.6% of mapped places against 8.1% in Hyderabad — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 1.8% of mapped places against 2.8% in Hyderabad — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 2.2% of mapped places against 3.5% in Hyderabad — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
